title: The pipeline.config.json architectural-tier trigger: a hardcoded floor, config-union-only, and what evaluates it
content:
Landed at #21 (merged to main as cab267f, PR #81), correcting a prior state where `pipeline.config.json`'s `architecturalTriggers` key had ZERO runtime readers of any sub-key anywhere in plugins/pipeline/scripts or plugins/pipeline/hooks (measured with a non-zero grep control), while commands/pipeline.md asserted in bold that a diff touching the file is 'architectural, always' and cited the key as the mechanism.

CURRENT SHAPE, FLOOR-PLUS-UNION: `agents/ba.md` Phase 1 duty 6 carries a hardcoded floor -- `paths: ["pipeline.config.json"]`, `domains: ["data","security","compliance"]`, and eight built-in keyword phrases (schema migration, data-access-policy change, shared contract shape change, auth flow, crypto, webhook verification, new external data intake, new retained data type) -- and a MARKER-FREE paragraph immediately after it instructing BA to read `architecturalTriggers.paths/domains/keywords` from the project's live `pipeline.config.json` at the project root (never the plugin cache) and UNION each sub-key onto the matching built-in list, per key, never pooled: a config value can only ADD a trigger, never remove one already listed. If the file is absent, fails to parse, or parses to anything other than a JSON object, treat it as `{}` and use the built-in floor alone; in every case, never name the config as the source of a trigger not actually read there. This repo's OWN live `pipeline.config.json` currently sets `architecturalTriggers.domains: ["security","compliance"]` (2 entries, missing `data`) -- under the shipped union rule `data` is STILL a forced trigger (floor holds); under a naive REPLACE reading it would be silently dropped. That is the load-bearing on-disk proof the floor is not decorative.

WIDEN-ONLY IS A FUNCTION PROPERTY, NOT A KEY PROPERTY -- record this at the correct grain, because #21 is the SECOND issue in a row where a citation at the wrong grain was the defect. The prose's own halting-control analogy names the function `migrationGlobsForTripwire` (unions, widen-only) and explicitly NOT its sibling `migrationGlobsForGate` (REPLACES on the exact same config key). Measured: tripwire narrowed stays at 15 globs under a narrowing config input; gate drops to 0 (empty config array) or to 1 (narrowing config) under the same input. A future restatement of 'widen-only' at the KEY grain ('the migrationGlobs key is widen-only') teaches the opposite of the truth for half the readers of that key. State every widen-vs-replace guarantee against the function/resolver name, never the bare config key.

TWO EVALUATORS TODAY, NO PATH-DIFF PREDICATE: (1) BA at Phase 1 intake, against the floor-plus-union set, before any diff exists; (2) the orchestrator's post-BA validation clause in commands/pipeline.md's `### Risk-tiered orchestration depth` section, immediately after BA returns, re-checking `spec.impacted_domains` against `{data,security,compliance}` or the same floor-plus-union path/keyword set, and promoting-and-logging if BA under-tiered. NEITHER evaluates a live diff: the mis-tier tripwire's glob set does not match `pipeline.config.json`, so a diff that touches this file WITHOUT having been named at intake is caught only by an agent-reported backstop, not a script -- one bullet each in `agents/dev.md` (its own nesting-level bullet, sited next to the existing tripwire bullet) and `agents/secops.md` (sited directly after the five-axis TRIPWIRE bullet, inside the `BEGIN/END STANDARD-TIER CONSTRAINTS` markers so it reaches the standard-tier Dev thread). Both backstop bullets cite #76, the deferred mechanical seat over the Phase 3-to-4 changed-path list, which this repo does not yet have. `scripts/config-doctor.mjs`'s `PROSE_KEYS.architecturalTriggers.reader` string names both prose evaluators and their file:section (`agents/ba.md Phase 1 duty 6` and `commands/pipeline.md ### Risk-tiered orchestration depth`) so a config auditor knows this key is judged by prose, not enforced by code -- purely descriptive, catches no drift by itself.

BOLD SENTENCE PRESERVED BYTE-IDENTICAL: 'A diff that touches `pipeline.config.json` itself is architectural, always' in commands/pipeline.md is unchanged at both origin/main refs across #21; only the PARENTHETICAL after it changed, now pointing at ba.md's built-in floor (a pointer) rather than restating the widen-only rule a second time (a copy that could drift from its target -- the exact idiom-drift shape this repo has already paid for at #40's ten-copy digest).

KNOWN GAPS CARRIED FORWARD, NOT DISCHARGED BY THIS RUN: AC15 in #21's verification record is PARTIAL by design -- one battery cell (AC15b.pipeline-md-hunks) could not run at Phase 3 because it crashed the battery on an unquoted `git diff -U0` hunk-header parse of a single-line hunk (`@@ -125 +125 @@`, git omits `,count` for a one-line hunk); QA repaired its own parser in Phase 4 and the criterion was independently hand-verified both ways (see knowledge/living-context/testing--qa-battery-hunk-header-parsing.json for the reusable bug). Two further battery cells (`AC8a.evaluators-named`, `AC6.matrix-recorded`) are recorded in impl-report.json's `known_instrument_gaps` as passing for the wrong reason; a future reader must not read #21's 59/59 (post-Phase-4-repair) green as covering them without re-reading that block. #76 (mechanical seat over the Phase 3-to-4 changed-path list) and the SecOps-deferred second seat for the trust-void condition (checkCommand read from the same file at the same trust level) remain open and are NOT this file's to close.
